title: Phase 5B: inference-only ablations of the Opus 5.5 frontier adapters on their existing Pair-A checkpoints

harness.benchmark: study.contracts_2026.inference_benchmark (trusted tree /opt/autopareto_trusted, runtime /opt/autopareto_runtime), candidate-only mode: precision-aware correctness, 20 s discarded warm-up, 8 windows of >= 8 s cached decode
harness.benchmark_sha256: must equal the evaluator_sha256 recorded by Phase 2A
harness.workload: 8 registered 1,024-token prompts, 128 greedy tokens, batch 1, bf16 autocast

variants.V1_no_cuda_graph: no per-prompt CUDA-graph capture; the same compiled regions launched eagerly per token; one warm-up per adapter
variants.V2_no_fusion: CUDA graph kept; decode regions and split-key attention run as the same pure Python functions without torch.compile (unfused aten kernels)
variants.V3_sdpa_attention: CUDA graph and fused regions kept; decode attention = masked SDPA over the static buffers (Opus's pre-attempt-18 kernel)
variants.V4_eager_unfused: no CUDA graph and no fusion: Opus's decode math as plain eager aten ops
variants.V5_linear_kv_cache: CUDA graph and fusion kept; sliding-window layers store a full-length linear K/V buffer restricted by the same window mask instead of a 272-slot ring

excluded: window-size changes (they change the trained function and would need retraining); any architectural change

kernel_census.scope: attempt 23 x 6 variants + baseline, after all timing runs; 32 profiled decode tokens after 8 warm-up tokens; diagnostic only

order_design: Two repeats per (checkpoint, variant): repeat 1 in forward order (23, 24, 27; V0..V5), repeat 2 fully reversed, so every variant's mean position is the same; the baseline runs at the start, middle and end. Each run is a separate process.
outcomes_per_run: decode tokens/s (cached_decode_tokens_per_second_median, 8 windows) and the frozen stability classification
end-to-end tokens/s = 128 / (prefill + 127-token decode), median over measured repetitions
peak allocated inference memory and K/V cache bytes
precision-aware correctness (passed; bf16 fast path or FP32 adjudication; max logit difference)

analysis.per_cell: mean of the two repeats (and both values) for every outcome
analysis.ratios: each variant relative to V0 of the same checkpoint; V0 and V4 relative to the same-session baseline
analysis.decomposition: decode time per token: graph factor = V0/V1, fusion factor = V0/V2, joint = V0/V4, interaction = joint/(graph x fusion); attention-kernel factor = V0/V3; ring-buffer factor = V0/V5 (speed) and V5/V0 (K/V bytes, peak memory); architecture-under-eager-execution factor = V4/baseline
analysis.end_to_end: the same factors for prefill ms and end-to-end tokens/s; report which variant maximises end-to-end throughput
analysis.stability: runs failing the frozen stability rule are reported, not re-run; no threshold is changed
analysis.significance: no significance tests; two repeats show the range. Effects are described as multiplicative factors with both repeats.

predictions_recorded_before_measurement: P1: removing the CUDA graph (V1) lowers decode throughput by more than 3x
P2: V1 prefill is below 0.3x V0 prefill (the per-prompt capture dominates V0 prefill)
P3: removing fusion (V2) lowers decode throughput, by less than the graph removal
P4: SDPA attention (V3) lowers decode throughput relative to V0
P5: the linear K/V cache (V5) has a larger K/V footprint and decode throughput within 15% of V0
P6: V4 (eager unfused Opus) decodes faster than the eager baseline, because it has 3 layers instead of 8
